result.description:
If you’re hoping to find somewhere to spend your weekends leisurely exploring the range of beaches, or lying in a hammock enjoying the warm weather, then Broome might be the place for you.

We are now recruiting for a full-time Early Childhood Teacher to join our amazing team in Roebuck - Broome WA!

Broome is located in the North of Western Australia and promotes an easy going culture with a tropical climate. It's rich past history has created a wonderful community complementing the colourful natural fauna and pristine beaches it is known for.

Our centre has 5 beautiful and spacious rooms that allow us to split our age groups more effectively. Our newly-renovated yards allow children to play outdoors at all times - rain or shine. Head to our website www.mulberrytree.com.au and check out our beautiful centre.

Company benefits:

10% above award wage
95% discount on your childcare fees. (conditions apply)
Rent assistance.
Generous Staff Appreciation budgets at each centre to strengthen relationships and reward our teams, including decadent morning teas, dinners and much more.
CPR Courses organised and paid for by head office (course fees and time attended).
Support and availability of a WA based Senior Management Team.
Relationship centred environments.
3 hours a week of non-contact.
Paid professional development courses.
Uniform allocations (annual).
Flexible work life balance.
Opportunities to further develop your career.
Continual mentoring from experienced Colleagues.
Opportunity to travel (centres located in Perth).

Who you are:

We are looking for leaders who promote children's education through their interests and planned learning opportunities. You will foster children's curiosity and create opportunities for children to grow and explore in small groups. The ideal candidate will value the wonders of early learning within our upcycled learning environments and guide staff in providing a fun, safe, high-quality service that aligns with the National Quality Standards and is true to Mulberry Tree Childcare's fantastic reputation. We embrace our children's love for learning and want you to concentrate on developing each child's trust and sense of security.

Criteria:

Bachelor of Early Childhood / Grad Diploma of Education (Early Childhood) / Bachelor in Education (Early Childhood) or ACECQA equivalent approved qualification OR be working towards your ECT qualification (50% of units finished).
Current Asthma, Anaphylaxis, CPR & First Aid certificates or willingness to obtain.
Current WWCC or willingness to obtain.
Knowledge and understanding of the Early Years Learning Framework / National Quality Framework / National Quality Standards / Belonging, Being and Becoming.
Understanding of Childcare Regulations and Law.

Ideal Candidate:

A strong level of communication skills and the ability to build strong relationships with staff, children, families and the community.
Be an inspiring leader and positive role model.
Have personal and professional aspirations to make the childcare industry that of a high professional standard.
Have a readiness to go above and beyond for the children and families.
Have a passion to make a difference in every child's learning Journey.
Be flexible, reliable and overall have a happy persona.
Want to make a difference in every child's life.

Who we are:

Mulberry Tree Childcare are a WA privately owned and operated family business that has supported WA children and families for 30 years. Our Mulberry Tree teams pride themselves in knowing that "Every moment in a child's life is a learning opportunity". Mulberry Tree are continually investing in their staff and centres and ensuring they are the best they can be.

To Apply:

Ready for an exciting change and to be part of an amazing team?

Apply today, by forwarding your resume to start your new venture!

Look forward to hearing from you.

result.description:
Cleaning Service Manager
Employer: Clear Wash Pty Ltd
Location: Gladesville, NSW (servicing commercial clients across Sydney)
Position: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: AUD $80,000 – $90,000 plus superannuation
About the Company
Clear Wash Pty Ltd is a growing commercial cleaning company providing professional cleaning services to offices, retail premises, medical facilities and commercial buildings throughout Sydney. We are committed to delivering reliable, high-quality cleaning services while maintaining excellent customer relationships and industry best practices.

We are seeking an experienced and motivated Cleaning Service Manager to oversee our commercial cleaning operations and ensure the efficient delivery of services across multiple client sites.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Promoting and selling Clear Wash's commercial cleaning services by building and maintaining strong relationships with existing and prospective clients and responding to service enquiries.
•	Planning, organising and coordinating day-to-day commercial cleaning operations, including staff allocations, cleaning schedules, equipment requirements and service delivery across multiple client sites and cleaning contracts.
•	Controlling the recruitment, induction, training, supervision and performance management of cleaning supervisors and cleaning staff to ensure quality service delivery.
•	Planning, sourcing, purchasing and managing cleaning chemicals, consumables and equipment and liaise with suppliers to ensure adequate stock levels and cost-effective procurement.
•	Developing, implementing and reviewing customer service procedures, operational policies and cleaning programs to continuously improve service quality and client satisfaction.
•	Establishing, implementing, monitoring and reviewing cleaning service standards, performance benchmarks and quality assurance measures, including site inspections and client feedback, to ensure contractual and company standards are consistently achieved.
•	Maintaining operational and financial records, preparing and managing operational budgets, monitoring labour costs, equipment expenditure and consumable usage, and implementing cost-control measures to ensure services are delivered within approved budgets.
•	Ensuring compliance with Work Health and Safety (WHS), chemical handling requirements, environmental regulations, infection control standards and other relevant legislation, company policies and industry standards.
•	Managing operational standards, including site security procedures, key management, housekeeping practices, equipment maintenance and quality assurance across all client sites.
•	Investigating and resolving customer enquiries, grievances or complaints and service issues promptly while maintaining strong ongoing client relationships.
•	Assisting the Directors in implementing business improvement initiatives and identifying opportunities to expand cleaning service contracts.
Essential Requirements
•	A relevant AQF Diploma or higher qualification (or overseas equivalent), or at least 3 years of relevant management experience in commercial cleaning, facilities management or a closely related service industry.
•	Demonstrated leadership and staff management experience.
•	Excellent organisational, communication and customer service skills.
•	Strong knowledge of commercial cleaning operations and quality assurance.
•	Sound understanding of Work Health and Safety legislation and compliance requirements.
•	A current Australian Driver Licence.
Salary
AUD $80,000 – $90,000 per annum plus superannuation, depending on qualifications and experience.
How to Apply
Please submit your resume together with a cover letter outlining your suitability for the position at luke@clearwash.com.au. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

result.description:
Location: Petrie, QLD, 4502
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Centre Manager & ECT
Job Title: Child Care Worker
Salary range: $79,500 - $86,600 - depending on skills level and work experience + superannuation.
Job Closure date: 30 days

About This Role:
Our client is a well-established early learning provider committed to nurturing children's growth through play-based learning and holistic development. With purpose-built facilities and a team of dedicated educators, they create warm, inclusive environments where children feel safe to explore, learn and thrive. Their philosophy emphasizes emotional wellbeing, creativity and foundational skill-building during these crucial early years. We're seeking a nurturing Childcare Worker to join their team. This role goes beyond supervision - you'll actively contribute to children's developmental milestones while fostering their curiosity through engaging, age-appropriate experiences.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Program Delivery & Child Development:
• Design and implement stimulating educational programs aligned with the Early Years Learning Framework (EYLF)
• Facilitate intentional teaching moments through play-based activities including storytelling, music, art and sensory exploration
• Observe and document children's progress to support individual learning goals and share insights with families
• Guide social-emotional development by modelling positive behaviour and conflict resolution strategies

Daily Care & Wellbeing:
• Maintain impeccable hygiene standards including nappy changing, toileting assistance and mealtime supervision
• Create predictable routines that provide children with emotional security while allowing flexibility for spontaneous learning
• Conduct thorough safety checks of indoor/outdoor environments and resources before activities
• Administer first aid when required and follow health management plans for children with additional needs

Family & Community Engagement:
• Build trusting relationships with families through daily conversations and formal progress updates
• Collaborate with room leaders to create displays that make children's learning visible to parents
• Participate in community events and centre initiatives that strengthen family connections

Compliance & Professionalism:
• Maintain current working with children check - first aid certification and relevant qualifications
• Contribute to quality improvement processes through reflective practice
• Attend staff meetings and professional development sessions to enhance practice

Skills & Requirements:
• Certificate III or Diploma in Early Childhood Education & Care (or ACECQA-approved equivalent)
• Proven 1-year minimum experience in long day care or similar setting.
• Demonstrated knowledge of EYLF and National Quality Standards
• Genuine passion for early childhood development with endless patience and creativity
• Current First Aid, Asthma & Anaphylaxis certificates as well as proof of vaccination
• Working with children rights
• Police check
• Strong communication skills to engage with children, colleagues and families
• References from previous employers

Why Apply?
This is more than a job - it's an opportunity to shape young lives in an environment that values educator wellbeing as much as child development. You'll receive:

• Above-award wages for qualified candidates
• Paid professional development opportunities
• Supportive leadership team with realistic expectations
• Purpose-built facilities with quality resources

If you're ready to make your mark in early childhood education with an organisation that values your expertise, we'd love to hear from you.

We are currently on the hunt for a Restaurant General Manager for Taco Bell Butler.

About the role

Restaurant Managers are legends in our business – from managing profits and losses, training, and inspiring team members to be the best they can be, to doing those little things that make shifts fun. Sharpen those management skills while benefiting from flexible hours, a competitive salary, great rewards, and a career path that could lead you to our corporate head office. You will grow at Taco Bell, while being celebrated for being yourself, and that feels pretty good.

Key Responsibilities of the role include:

- Responsible for execution of the WHS System. Ensure they are, and employees under their control, are observing safe work practices, safety procedures and that any hazardous situations are rendered safe. Ensuring all incidents are reported to WHS Officer.
- Manage the restaurant in accordance with Company Policies and Procedures, to Brand Standard. 
- Ensure that controls and procedures are implemented on each shift to protect the security of employees and company funds.
- Direct the activities of employees to maximize sales, operating efficiency, and profit, including determining product mix, maintaining stock levels, implementing purchasing and marketing policies and pricing.
- Allocate responsibilities to each employee on shift and monitor performance accordingly. Ensure tasks are only undertaken by those employees certified to perform them.
- Promote the Company’s goods and services by implementing customer service standards within the restaurant. Ensure the whole restaurant team is focused on exceeding customer expectations for Cleanliness, Hospitality, Accuracy, Maintenance, Product Quality and Speed of Service. 
- Implement the recruitment and selection process of employees within the restaurant.
- Implement restaurant training programs for Assistant Restaurant Managers, Shift leaders, and Team Members, to enable them to maximize performance, meet the standards, and realize their career potential. Monitor performance and implement corrective action where required. 
- Ensure that employees follow correct maintenance procedures in accordance with the established maintenance roster and advise the Restaurant General Manager of any repairs or maintenance required within the restaurant.
- Report to the Area Coach any aspect of employee relations/performance. 
- Report to the Area Coach any aspect of customer service, attendance of and/or inspections by third parties that have or are likely to affect the operation of the restaurant.
- Keep the Area Coach informed of any competitive activity that is likely to affect the trading results of the restaurant. 
- Promote the Company values, acting as a role model and always providing leadership.
- Monitor and coordinate the charge areas of the Assistant Restaurant Managers; ensuring Customer, Profit, Labour, Sales, Operations and People targets are met.

Decision Making Authority: 

Primary responsibility for the restaurant operation. 
- Hiring, managing, and terminating in accordance with Company Policy. 
- Approval of expenditure within the established guidelines.
- High School Certificate (HSC or equivalent) - essential. Tertiary Qualifications preferred.
- Minimum of 3 years multi outlet retail or service industry experience at a supervisory level (external candidates); 1 year for internal candidates. 
- Proven track record of On Target performance in Balanced Scorecard KPIs (or equivalent) with primary profit responsibility essential. 
- First Aid Certified: Apply First Aid – essential.
- Ability to engage, lead and motivate all restaurant employees to deliver KPI Targets.
 

Benefits:
Some of the benefits of this role include:

Base salary range $75,000 to $85,000
Bonus schemes and recognition culture that ensures that hard work and good performance is rewarded
Complete several our internal management courses including Restaurant Managers Academy
Participate in a world-class leadership program
Opportunity to progress into above store leadership roles in the operations field or at our Restaurant Support Centre.
 

An ideal candidate will have experience in a restaurant or retail environment. Management experience and a passion for people is necessary for a superstar candidate! You will be required to demonstrate your eligibility for full working rights in Australia.

result.description:
## Chief Information Officer
## Position Overview
We are looking for a visionary and commercially astute Chief Information Officer (CIO) to lead our organisation's information and communications technology strategy, operations, and governance. This is a senior executive role suited to an experienced technology leader who thrives at the intersection of business strategy and digital innovation. The successful candidate will be responsible for aligning ICT capabilities with organisational priorities, driving transformation, and ensuring the long-term integrity and security of our technology infrastructure.
## Key Responsibilities
- Analyse organisational information needs and define technology solutions that effectively support business objectives and operational performance
- Formulate, implement, and continuously refine ICT strategies, policies, and plans that align with the organisation's broader mission and priorities
- Lead the selection, procurement, and installation of ICT systems and infrastructure, ensuring solutions are scalable, reliable, and fit for purpose
- Direct ICT operations across the organisation, setting clear priorities between system development, ongoing maintenance, and day-to-day operations
- Oversee the organisation's cybersecurity posture, ensuring robust protections are in place to safeguard data, systems, and digital assets
- Drive digital transformation initiatives that improve organisational efficiency, enhance service delivery, and support innovation
- Develop and manage the ICT budget, ensuring effective allocation of resources and demonstrable return on technology investment
- Build, mentor, and lead high-performing ICT teams, fostering a culture of collaboration, continuous learning, and professional development
- Engage and manage relationships with external technology vendors, partners, and service providers to ensure contractual obligations and service standards are met
- Champion the rollout of user training programmes to ensure staff are equipped to effectively adopt and utilise ICT systems and tools
- Provide executive-level reporting and strategic advice to the Board and senior leadership team on technology risks, opportunities, and performance
- Ensure ICT systems and practices remain compliant with relevant legislation, industry standards, and data governance frameworks
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree or higher in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related discipline
- Demonstrated experience in a senior ICT leadership role, with a strong track record of delivering enterprise-wide technology strategy
- Proven ability to align ICT capability with organisational strategy and drive measurable business outcomes
- Strong understanding of cybersecurity principles, risk management, and data governance best practices
- Experience managing large-scale ICT budgets, procurement processes, and vendor relationships
- Excellent leadership and people management skills, with the ability to inspire, develop, and retain high-performing teams
- Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with a strategic mindset and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
- Sound knowledge of ICT infrastructure, cloud environments, enterprise systems, and emerging technologies
- High-level communication, negotiation, and stakeholder engagement skills across all levels of an organisation
## Preferred Qualifications
- Postgraduate qualification in Business Administration (MBA), Information Technology, or a related field
- Industry certifications such as ITIL, TOGAF, CISSP, or equivalent
- Experience leading digital transformation programmes within complex or large-scale organisations
- Familiarity with Australian data privacy legislation, including the Privacy Act 1988 and the Australian Privacy Principles
- Prior experience presenting to executive leadership teams or Boards of Directors
## Why Join Us?
- Play a pivotal role in shaping the digital future of a dynamic and growing organisation, with genuine influence at the executive level
- Access to ongoing professional development opportunities, including leadership programmes, industry conferences, and certifications
- Flexible working arrangements that support a healthy work-life balance
- Collaborative and inclusive workplace culture that values innovation, integrity, and continuous improvement
- Competitive remuneration package with performance-based incentives and additional employee benefits
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation
